stem: Solve for $x$: $-{=a}x {=sym} {=c}$. Which one of the following is the solution?
solution: To get $x$ on its own, divide both sides of $-{=a}x {=sym} {=c}$ by $-{=a}$.
Dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the inequality sign, so ${=sym}$ becomes ${=fsym}$.
Check with $x = {=t}$: $-{=a} \cdot ({=t}) = {=pv}$, and ${=pv} {=sym} {=c}$ is true, so the solution is $x {=fsym} {=s}$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Ignores the minus sign on the coefficient of x
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student reads $-ax$ as $ax$ and divides both sides by the positive number $a$, so the sign is not reversed and the boundary value comes out with the wrong sign (for example $-3x>12$ becomes $x>4$).

notes: Entry-point skill: one division by a negative coefficient, modelled on the book's own steps in ex4-6-2b (-3x <= 9 gives x >= -3), 2d and 2k, which divide by a negative number and reverse the sign. The inequality symbol is drawn as < or > (d), so the instances are not always answered with the same sign; coefficient a in 2..6 (a = 1 is left out so the stem never prints -1x), boundary s in -9..9 excluding 0 so the four options are always four different statements. The RHS is built backwards (c = -a*s) so the boundary is always a whole number and the working is exact. Options: correct x fsym s; keeps the sign (catalogued mc keeps-sign-after-negative); reads -ax as ax, giving x sym -s (new mc ignores-negative-coefficient); reverses the sign but divides the constant by +a, giving x fsym -s (no named error, null). Multiple choice is used because every wrong option is a specific sign error and the answer is an inequality; I did not use the plain interval marker for this family because I could not confirm how the marker syntax writes the infinite endpoint, and the book's interval-notation answers are all unbounded. Only the listed basic gap is filled. The book's standard exercises ask for interval notation, which needs that infinite-endpoint syntax confirmed, so no standard or advanced family was written.
